kind.quote: Has completed an approved residency of at least 1 year.

exams.name: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)
exams.notes: Passing score as established by rule of the board; prior examinations (FLEX, NBME) also accepted in combination up to year 2000; SPEX permitted for certain long-practicing licensees
exams.quote: Has obtained a passing score, as established by rule of the board, on the licensure examination of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)

interval_years.quote: The department shall adopt rules establishing a procedure for the biennial renewal of licenses.

required.quote: the Board of Medicine … shall each require licensees which they respectively regulate to periodically demonstrate their professional competency by completing at least 40 hours of continuing education every 2 years.

hours_per_period.quote: completing at least 40 hours of continuing education every 2 years.

period_years.quote: completing at least 40 hours of continuing education every 2 years.

value: 2-hour course on prevention of medical errors (including root-cause analysis, error reduction and prevention, patient safety, and five most misdiagnosed conditions)
2-hour course on prescribing controlled substances (for DEA registrants)
2-hour course on domestic violence (every third biennial renewal)
1-hour course on HIV and AIDS (at first renewal)
topical_requirements.quote: The boards, or the department when there is no board, shall require the completion of a 2-hour course relating to prevention of medical errors as part of the biennial renewal process.

available.quote: The department shall issue a license by endorsement to any applicant who, upon applying to the department on forms furnished by the department and remitting a fee set by the board in an amount not to exceed $500, the board certifies has: (1) Met the requirements for licensure by endorsement under s. 456.0145

requirements.value: Must meet requirements of the MOBILE Act (s. 456.0145): active unencumbered out-of-state license, national exam/certification or substantially similar requirements, 2 years of active practice in preceding 4 years, no pending disciplinary proceedings, no adverse disciplinary action in last 5 years, financial responsibility, fingerprints. Alternatively, may meet endorsement requirements except for recency-of-practice with board-approved postgraduate training or competency exam.
requirements.quote: Met the requirements for licensure by endorsement under s. 456.0145; or Met the requirements for licensure by endorsement under s. 456.0145 except for s. 456.0145(2)(a)4. but has submitted evidence to the board's satisfaction of the successful completion of either a board-approved postgraduate training program within 2 years preceding the filing of an application or a board-approved clinical competency examination within the year preceding the filing of an application.

exists.quote: There is created within the department the Board of Medicine, composed of 15 members appointed by the Governor and confirmed by the Senate.

national_certification.value: National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME); Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG)
national_certification.quote: has had his or her medical credentials evaluated by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates, holds an active, valid certificate issued by that commission, and has passed the examination utilized by that commission

national_association.value: American Board of Medical Specialties; American Medical Association (Council on Medical Education)
national_association.quote: fellowship experience and training must be counted toward regular or subspecialty certification by a board recognized and certified by the American Board of Medical Specialties

regulatory_model.quote: The practice of medicine or an attempt to practice medicine without a license to practice in Florida.

credential_type.quote: Each applicant who meets the requirements of this chapter shall be licensed as a physician, with rights as defined by law.

is_mandatory.quote: The practice of medicine or an attempt to practice medicine without a license to practice in Florida.

title_protection.quote: Leading the public to believe that one is licensed as a medical doctor, or is engaged in the licensed practice of medicine, without holding a valid, active license.

scope_protection.quote: The practice of medicine or an attempt to practice medicine without a license to practice in Florida.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Attempting to obtain, obtaining, or renewing a license by bribery, fraudulent misrepresentation, or error of the department or board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Attempting to obtain, obtaining, or renewing a license to practice medicine by bribery, by fraudulent misrepresentations, or through an error of the department or the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having a license revoked, suspended, or otherwise acted against by any licensing authority in any jurisdiction.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having a license or the authority to practice medicine revoked, suspended, or otherwise acted against, including the denial of licensure, by the licensing authority of any jurisdiction, including its agencies or subdivisions.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being convicted of or pleading nolo contendere to a crime that directly relates to the practice of medicine or ability to practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being convicted or found guilty of, or entering a plea of nolo contendere to, regardless of adjudication, a crime in any jurisdiction which directly relates to the practice of medicine or to the ability to practice medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: False, deceptive, or misleading advertising.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: False, deceptive, or misleading advertising.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to report to the department any person the licensee knows is violating the chapter or board rules.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the department any person who the licensee knows is in violation of this chapter or of the rules of the department or the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding, assisting, procuring, or advising any unlicensed person to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding, assisting, procuring, or advising any unlicensed person to practice medicine contrary to this chapter or to a rule of the department or the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to perform any statutory or legal obligation placed upon a licensed physician.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to perform any statutory or legal obligation placed upon a licensed physician.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making or filing a report known to be false, or failing to file a required report.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making or filing a report which the licensee knows to be false, intentionally or negligently failing to file a report or record required by state or federal law

disciplinary_grounds.description: Paying or receiving commissions, kickbacks, or rebates for patient referrals.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Paying or receiving any commission, bonus, kickback, or rebate, or engaging in any split-fee arrangement in any form whatsoever with a physician, organization, agency, or person, either directly or indirectly, for patients referred to providers of health care goods and services

disciplinary_grounds.description: Exercising influence within a patient-physician relationship for purposes of engaging a patient in sexual activity.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Exercising influence within a patient-physician relationship for purposes of engaging a patient in sexual activity.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representations in or related to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representations in or related to the practice of medicine or employing a trick or scheme in the practice of medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Soliciting patients through the use of fraud, intimidation, or undue influence.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Soliciting patients, either personally or through an agent, through the use of fraud, intimidation, undue influence, or a form of overreaching or vexatious conduct.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to keep legible medical records that justify the course of treatment.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to keep legible, as defined by department rule in consultation with the board, medical records that identify the licensed physician or the physician extender and supervising physician by name and professional title who is or are responsible for rendering, ordering, supervising, or billing for each diagnostic or treatment procedure and that justify the course of treatment of the patient

disciplinary_grounds.description: Exercising influence on the patient to exploit them for financial gain.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Exercising influence on the patient or client in such a manner as to exploit the patient or client for financial gain of the licensee or of a third party

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing professional services not duly authorized by the patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Performing professional services which have not been duly authorized by the patient or client, or his or her legal representative

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, dispensing, or administering a legend drug including controlled substances other than in the course of professional practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, dispensing, administering, mixing, or otherwise preparing a legend drug, including any controlled substance, other than in the course of the physician's professional practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, dispensing, or administering any medicinal drug to oneself.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, dispensing, or administering any medicinal drug appearing on any schedule set forth in chapter 893 by the physician to himself or herself

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being unable to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety to patients due to illness, substance use, or mental/physical condition.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being unable to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness or use of alcohol, drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or any other type of material or as a result of any mental or physical condition.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Committing medical malpractice, gross medical malpractice, or repeated medical malpractice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Committing medical malpractice as defined in s. 456.50.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing any procedure or prescribing therapy that constitutes experimentation on a human subject without informed consent.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Performing any procedure or prescribing any therapy which, by the prevailing standards of medical practice in the community, would constitute experimentation on a human subject, without first obtaining full, informed, and written consent.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing or offering to practice beyond the scope permitted by law or performing services the licensee is not competent to perform.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing or offering to practice beyond the scope permitted by law or accepting and performing professional responsibilities which the licensee knows or has reason to know that he or she is not competent to perform.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Delegating professional responsibilities to a person not qualified by training, experience, or licensure.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Delegating professional responsibilities to a person when the licensee delegating such responsibilities knows or has reason to know that such person is not qualified by training, experience, or licensure to perform them.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating a lawful order of the board or department or failing to comply with a subpoena.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating a lawful order of the board or department previously entered in a disciplinary hearing or failing to comply with a lawfully issued subpoena of the department.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Procuring, or aiding in procuring, an unlawful termination of pregnancy.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Procuring, or aiding or abetting in the procuring of, an unlawful termination of pregnancy.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Presigning blank prescription forms.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Presigning blank prescription forms.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing Schedule II amphetamines or sympathomimetic amines except for specified conditions.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, ordering, dispensing, administering, supplying, selling, or giving any drug which is a Schedule II amphetamine or a Schedule II sympathomimetic amine drug or any compound thereof, pursuant to chapter 893, to or for any person except for: [specified conditions]

approximate.matched_normalized: prescribing ordering dispensing administering supplying selling or giving any drug which is a schedule ii amphetamine or a schedule ii sympathomimetic amine drug or any compound thereof pursuant to chapter 893 to or for any person except for

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to supervise adequately physician assistants and other practitioners acting under supervision.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to supervise adequately the activities of those physician assistants, paramedics, emergency medical technicians, advanced practice registered nurses, or anesthesiologist assistants acting under the supervision of the physician.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing growth hormones, testosterone, HCG, or other hormones for muscle building or athletic performance enhancement.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, ordering, dispensing, administering, supplying, selling, or giving growth hormones, testosterone or its analogs, human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG), or other hormones for the purpose of muscle building or to enhance athletic performance.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Misrepresenting or concealing a material fact during any phase of a licensing or disciplinary process.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Misrepresenting or concealing a material fact at any time during any phase of a licensing or disciplinary process or procedure.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Improperly interfering with an investigation or disciplinary proceeding.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Improperly interfering with an investigation or with any disciplinary proceeding.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to report a licensee known to have violated grounds for disciplinary action in a shared facility.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the board, in writing, within 30 days if action as defined in paragraph (b) has been taken against one's license to practice medicine in another state, territory, or country.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising or holding oneself out as a board-certified specialist when not qualified.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising or holding oneself out as a board-certified specialist, if not qualified under s. 458.3312, in violation of this chapter.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to comply with requirements to provide patients with information about their rights.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to comply with the requirements of ss. 381.026 and 381.0261 to provide patients with information about their patient rights and how to file a patient complaint.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating any provision of chapter 458, chapter 456, or rules adopted pursuant thereto.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating any provision of this chapter or chapter 456, or any rules adopted pursuant thereto.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Providing deceptive or fraudulent expert witness testimony related to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Providing deceptive or fraudulent expert witness testimony related to the practice of medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Various violations relating to pain-management clinic registration and operation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Registering a pain-management clinic through misrepresentation or fraud

disciplinary_grounds.description: Sexual misconduct in the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Sexual misconduct in the practice of medicine means violation of the physician-patient relationship through which the physician uses said relationship to induce or attempt to induce the patient to engage, or to engage or attempt to engage the patient, in sexual activity outside the scope of the practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Implanting a patient with a human embryo or inseminating a patient with the licensee's own reproductive material.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Implanting a patient or causing a patient to be implanted with a human embryo created with the human reproductive material, as defined in s. 784.086, of the licensee, or inseminating a patient or causing a patient to be inseminated with the human reproductive material of the licensee.

insurance_required.quote: Obtaining and maintaining professional liability coverage in an amount not less than $100,000 per claim, with a minimum annual aggregate of not less than $300,000

establishment_regulation_required.quote: Each pain-management clinic must register with the department or hold a valid certificate of exemption pursuant to subsection (2).

definition_quote.value: The diagnosis, treatment, operation, or prescription for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity, or other physical or mental condition.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine" means the diagnosis, treatment, operation, or prescription for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity, or other physical or mental condition.

methods_authorized.quote: "Practice of medicine" means the diagnosis, treatment, operation, or prescription for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity, or other physical or mental condition.

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe, dispense, and administer legend drugs including controlled substances in Schedules II-V in the course of professional practice; may prescribe Schedule II-V controlled substances for treatment of intractable pain; opioid prescriptions for acute pain generally limited to 3-day supply (up to 7 days with documented justification). DEA registrants must complete CE on controlled substance prescribing.
drug_authority.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a physician may prescribe or administer any controlled substance under Schedules II-V, as provided for in s. 893.03, to a person for the treatment of intractable pain, provided the physician does so in accordance with that level of care, skill, and treatment recognized by a reasonably prudent physician under similar conditions and circumstances.

license_status_types.quote: A license that has become inactive may be reactivated under s. 458.319 upon application to the department.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must either: (1) graduate from a WHO-registered foreign medical school certified under s. 458.314 as meeting US accreditation standards, pass an English proficiency requirement if not taught in English, and complete at least 1 year of approved residency; or (2) graduate from an uncertified foreign medical school, obtain ECFMG evaluation and certificate, pass ECFMG exam, and complete at least 2 years of approved residency or fellowship after October 1, 1992. Exception exists for certain foreign graduates with US bachelor's degrees who complete supervised clinical training.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Is a graduate of an allopathic foreign medical school registered with the World Health Organization and certified pursuant to s. 458.314 as having met the standards required to accredit medical schools in the United States or reasonably comparable standards

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Has completed an approved residency of at least 1 year.

pain_management_education_required.quote: each person registered with the United States Drug Enforcement Administration and authorized to prescribe controlled substances pursuant to 21 U.S.C. s. 822 to complete a board-approved 2-hour continuing education course on prescribing controlled substances

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: For acute pain, opioid prescriptions (Schedule II) may not exceed a 3-day supply; up to 7-day supply may be prescribed if clinically justified and documented with 'ACUTE PAIN EXCEPTION' noted. For non-acute pain, prescriber must indicate 'NONACUTE PAIN' on Schedule II opioid prescriptions. For traumatic injuries with ISS ≥9, concurrent prescription of emergency opioid antagonist required.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: For the treatment of acute pain, a prescription for an opioid drug listed as a Schedule II controlled substance in s. 893.03 or 21 U.S.C. s. 812 may not exceed a 3-day supply

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: A physician authorized to prescribe controlled substances who practices at a pain-management clinic is responsible for maintaining the control and security of his or her prescription blanks or electronic prescribing software used for prescribing controlled substance pain medication.

pain_management_clinic_registration_requ.quote: Each pain-management clinic must register with the department or hold a valid certificate of exemption pursuant to subsection (2).

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Telehealth providers may not prescribe Schedule II controlled substances via telehealth unless for treatment of a psychiatric disorder, inpatient hospital treatment, hospice services, or nursing home residents. Telehealth providers must practice consistent with prevailing professional standard of care and may not perform abortions via telehealth.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: A telehealth provider may not use telehealth to prescribe a controlled substance listed in Schedule II of s. 893.03 unless the controlled substance is prescribed for the following: 1. The treatment of a psychiatric disorder; 2. Inpatient treatment at a hospital licensed under chapter 395; 3. The treatment of a patient receiving hospice services as defined in s. 400.601; or 4. The treatment of a resident of a nursing home facility as defined in s. 400.021.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: A health care professional not licensed in this state may provide health care services to a patient located in this state using telehealth if the health care professional registers with the applicable board

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The Interstate Medical Licensure Compact is hereby enacted into law and entered into by this state with all other jurisdictions legally joining therein

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: Except in cases of emergency, supervision requires the easy availability or physical presence of the licensed physician for consultation and direction of the actions of the physician assistant.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A supervising physician may delegate to a fully licensed physician assistant authority to prescribe or dispense any medication used in the supervising physician's practice except those on a restricted formulary. Schedule II controlled substances limited to 7-day supply (14-day for Schedule II psychiatric mental health controlled substances for children under 18). General anesthetics and radiographic contrast materials prohibited. PA must complete 10 CE hours in specialty practice per renewal, including 3 hours on safe and effective prescribing of controlled substances.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A supervising physician may delegate to a fully licensed physician assistant, pursuant to a written protocol, the authority to prescribe or dispense any medication used in the supervising physician's practice unless such medication is listed on the formulary created pursuant to paragraph (f).

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: A physician may not supervise more than 10 currently licensed physician assistants at any one time.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Any practitioner of medicine licensed pursuant to the provisions of chapter 458 … shall report to the Office of Insurance Regulation any claim or action for damages for personal injury alleged to have been caused by error, omission, or negligence in the performance of such licensee's professional services

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Has been disciplined by a licensed hospital, health maintenance organization, prepaid health clinic, ambulatory surgical center, or nursing home or the medical staff of such a hospital … for any act that constitutes a violation of this chapter. If a physician resigns or withdraws from privileges when such facility notifies the physician that it is conducting an investigation … the facility shall complete its investigation or inquiry and shall notify the department

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The department may retain one or more consultants to operate its impaired practitioner program.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: the department shall have, upon a finding of the State Surgeon General or the State Surgeon General's designee that probable cause exists to believe that the licensee is unable to practice medicine because of the reasons stated in this paragraph, the authority to issue an order to compel a licensee to submit to a mental or physical examination by physicians designated by the department.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: "Actively practiced medicine" means that practice of medicine by physicians, including those employed by any governmental entity in community or public health, as defined by this chapter, including physicians practicing administrative medicine.

sexual_misconduct_training_required.quote: Sexual misconduct in the practice of medicine is prohibited.

investigational_drug_protection.quote: No physician shall be subject to disciplinary action by the Board of Medicine or Board of Osteopathic Medicine for prescribing or administering dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to a patient under his or her care who has requested the substance.

scope__license_status_types.quote: A license that has become inactive may be reactivated under s. 458.319 upon application to the department.
Each board, or the department if there is no board, shall permit a licensee to choose, at the time of licensure renewal, an active, inactive, or retired status.
A physician licensed to practice in any jurisdiction of the United States whose license is currently valid may be issued a temporary certificate for practice in areas of critical need.
The Board of Medicine may, by rule, develop criteria and, without examination, issue restricted licenses annually to up to 100 persons to practice medicine in this state

Certification to the department of an application for licensure, certification, or registration with placement of the physician on probation for a period of time and subject to such conditions as the board may specify

The department shall issue an emergency order suspending the license of any health care practitioner who pleads guilty to, is convicted or found guilty of, or enters a plea of nolo contendere to, regardless of adjudication, any of the following

The board may enter an order denying licensure or imposing any of the penalties in s. 456.072(2) against any applicant for licensure or licensee who is found guilty of violating any provision of subsection (1)

The licensing authority's acceptance of a physician's relinquishment of a license, stipulation, consent order, or other settlement, offered in response to or in anticipation of the filing of administrative charges against the physician's license, shall be construed as action against the physician's license.
A medical faculty certificate may be issued without examination to an individual who meets all of the following criteria

Any person holding an active license to practice medicine in this state may convert that license to a limited license under this subsection for the purpose of providing volunteer, uncompensated care for low-income Floridians.
A physician licensed to practice allopathic medicine under s. 456.4501 is deemed to also be licensed under this chapter.

Any person desiring to practice as a resident physician, assistant resident physician, house physician, intern, or fellow in fellowship training … who does not hold a valid, active license issued under this chapter shall apply to the department to be registered

A graduate assistant physician is a medical school graduate who meets the requirements of this subsection and has obtained a limited license from the board for the purpose of practicing temporarily under the direct supervision of a physician
